title: Soledad Mountain
text: Soledad Mountain rises just south of Mojave, and gold was first found there in 1894, when prospectors chased the Queen Esther and other veins. In 1933, George Holmes struck the Silver Queen vein, which revived mining across the district and drew in investors from South Africa. The Golden Queen Mining Company was organized in 1935 to consolidate four of the mountain's mines. The mines produced more than 10 million dollars from 1894 to 1942, before a federal wartime order shut down gold mining. By 2016, the mountain had reopened as a modern open-pit, heap-leach mine.
